workflowRecommendation: One implementer, one pull request, tasks in the order below (T1 -> T5 are a dependency chain; T6 docs and T7 skill are independent of the code and can be done at any point). Work test-first inside each task: change the pinned test, watch it fail, make the code change. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` from packages/daemon after T2 to find every remaining `string` use of the old pendingAssignment; the compiler is the checklist for the plumbing. Do not touch the 62 `processes.spawnWorker(...)` test call sites: the public signature is kept on purpose.
concerns: Sub-architect exemption (recorded in the spec, New since we talked, version 4): `resumeWorker` is the ONLY recovery path for a child issue's architect (`handleException` sends the root architect to `resurrect`), and a sub-architect is never `phases[child].phase` once it has spawned a planner. Applying Acceptance 7's not-sent rule to `role === "architect"` would strand every dead sub-architect forever. Exempt it exactly as `retireIdleWorker` does (`if (claim.role === "architect")`); processes.test.ts:5505 is the regression lock.

Every existing `handleException` test for a phase-worker role (processes.test.ts 3134, 3178, 3242, 3295, and the one at 3398 if it reaches resumeWorker) currently has NO `state.phases[<issue>]` fixture. Under the new eligibility rule they would silently skip the catch-up and fail on their prompt/--resume assertions. Each gains `state.phases[<issue>] = { phase: <role>, sessionId: <the claim's sessionId> }` so the role is the active phase; that is the real-world shape (the active phase's worker died).

Race the in-lock guard exists for: `resumeWorker` reads the claim, then awaits `workerCatchup` (a GitHub fetch, seconds), then `deliverToWorker` takes the per-role lock. An architect `spawn_worker` landing in that window puts an `assignment` on the booting claim; without the guard inside the lock the catch-up would overwrite it (Acceptance 8). The `resumeWorker` pre-check is only an optimisation that skips the fetch; the lock-side check is the invariant. Test it deterministically by mutating the claim from the test's `workerCatchup.tokenManager.getToken` hook (the `manager()` fixture spreads `overrides` after its default `workerCatchup`, so a test can replace it).

Between a freshly assigned role's `/worker/started` and its `/worker/ready`, `phases[issue]` still names the previous phase (or nothing) and events route there. The spec accepts this (Acceptance 2: 'once that assignment reaches it'); do not add an interim write.

A `catchup` left queued on a claim (at the worker cap, or booting) whose role then stopped being the active phase is still delivered on promotion/ready. It is harmless (a catchup never writes the phase) and the spec does not ask to prune it; leave it.

legion-state.test.ts:614-678 (the v19 -> v20 backfill test) has a `pendingAssignment: "verify #41"` string fixture inside a pre-v24 file. The v24 -> v25 migration classifies it; the test's `toEqual` for that claim must expect `{ kind: "assignment", task: "verify #41" }` (or the fixture must be written in the new object form, which the migration must pass through untouched: only `typeof pendingAssignment === "string"` is migrated).
Migration `JSON.parse` must never throw on an architect task (free text): wrap it; a non-JSON string is an assignment. Only `recordValue(parsed) && parsed.type === "catchup-worker"` is a catchup.

`docs/solutions/daemon/external-red-and-phase-ownership.md` section 2 and `idle-expiry-timers-rearm-on-declines-that-change-while-idle.md` describe `/worker/started` as a `phases[issue]` writer. They are learnings, owned by retro, not code comments: leave them; retro decides whether to add a note.

`LEGION_DAEMON_API_VERSION` does NOT bump: no `LegionDaemonApi` request/response shape changes (`/state` never exposed `pendingAssignment`; `spawn_worker`'s request still carries a plain `task` string).

Tester lever for a real-daemon E2E (not a unit test): the daemon consumes `notifications.envoy.exceptions.<role topic>` envelopes into `handleException`. Publish a synthetic exception for a FINISHED role on an issue whose active phase is another role and observe via `legion state` that `phases[issue]` is unchanged and no pane was opened (one `[legion] no catch-up for ...` log line). Negative control: kill the ACTIVE phase's pane, publish the same exception for its role, observe a `--resume` relaunch whose claim carries `pendingAssignment: { kind: "catchup", ... }` and, after ready, `phases[issue]` still names that role and session.

designDecisions.pendingAssignmentShape: `WorkerRoleClaim.pendingAssignment?: PendingAssignment` where `export interface PendingAssignment { kind: "assignment" | "catchup"; task: string }` (legion-state.ts, beside WorkerRoleClaim). One slot, discriminated: every reader is forced by the type to say which kind it handles. Rejected: a sibling `pendingAssignmentKind` field (both-or-neither invariant not type-enforced) and two fields `pendingAssignment` + `pendingCatchup` (every reader needs a precedence rule; the spec says a catch-up is DROPPED when an assignment is pending, not stored beside it). Rejected: sniffing the string payload at delivery time with no schema change (an architect's free-text task can be JSON; the spec settled on a stored discriminator with a migration).
designDecisions.publicSignature: `ProcessManager.spawnWorker(treeKey, issue, role, task: string)` is unchanged (the `/worker/spawn` route, `api.ts`'s ProcessManager interface, and 62 test call sites). It becomes a one-line wrapper: `return this.deliverToWorker(treeKey, issue, role, { kind: "assignment", task })`. The current body moves verbatim into `private async deliverToWorker(treeKey, issue, role, pending: PendingAssignment): Promise<SpawnWorkerResponse>`. `resumeWorker` calls `deliverToWorker(root, issue, role, { kind: "catchup", task: JSON.stringify(catchup) })`.
designDecisions.oneWriter: `state.phases[issue]` is written by exactly one statement: `promptExistingWorker`, and only when `pending.kind === "assignment"`. That covers both architect-assignment deliveries (prompted straight into a live worker via `resumeOrQueueExisting`/queue promotion, or delivered from `pendingAssignment` at `/worker/ready`). Role-agnostic, as today (a sub-architect's assignment still makes it `phases[child]`).
designDecisions.activePhasePredicate: `export function isActivePhase(state: LegionState, issue: IssueKey, role: string): boolean` in legion-state.ts: `phases[issue]` defined, `!completed`, `phase === role`. Used by `retireIdleWorker` (replacing its inline predicate), `resumeWorker`, and `handleWorkerStarted`'s log condition. `routeActive` keeps its own code (it needs the phase object).
designDecisions.catchupEligibility: In `resumeWorker`, after the existing no-claim guard and before `workerCatchup`: (a) `claim.pendingAssignment?.kind === "assignment"` -> log `dropping catch-up for <token>: the architect's assignment is queued and reaches the worker first`, return; (b) `role !== "architect" && !isActivePhase(state, issue, role) && claim.pendingAssignment === undefined` -> log `no catch-up for <token>: <issue>'s active phase is <phase|none> and nothing is queued for this role; only spawn_worker resumes a finished worker`, return. Plus the lock-side invariant at the top of `deliverToWorker`'s `mutateClaim` callback right after `const claim = ...`: `if (pending.kind === "catchup" && claim?.pendingAssignment?.kind === "assignment") { log; return { status: "resumed", roleToken: token }; }` -- covers all three pendingAssignment write sites (booting branch, enqueueIdleWorker, enqueueClaimForLaunch/launchWorker) under the race described in concerns.
designDecisions.workerStartedLog: `console.info` (the convention `retireIdleWorker` uses for a non-error lifecycle line), emitted only when `!isActivePhase(state, issue, role) && current.pendingAssignment?.kind !== "assignment"` -- a fresh spawn with its assignment queued is the normal path and must not log. Text names the token, session, issue, the current active phase (or `none`), and that only an architect assignment changes it.

tasks.title: State schema v25: PendingAssignment, migration, isActivePhase
steps: Add `export interface PendingAssignment { kind: "assignment" | "catchup"; task: string }` with a doc comment: `assignment` = an architect's spawn_worker task, the one delivery that makes its role the issue's active phase; `catchup` = the daemon's own `catchup-worker` recovery prompt (resumeWorker), which never changes the phase. Change `WorkerRoleClaim.pendingAssignment?: PendingAssignment`.

Zod: `const PendingAssignmentSchema = z.object({ kind: z.enum(["assignment", "catchup"]), task: z.string() }).strict();` and `pendingAssignment: PendingAssignmentSchema.optional()` in `WorkerRoleClaimSchema`.
Version 24 -> 25 in: `LegionState.version: 25`, `LegionStateSchema` `version: z.literal(25)`, `newLegionState`'s `version: 25`, `loadState`'s `if (version !== 25)` check.

Add `migrateV24State(state)` after `migrateV23State` and append it to the `migrations` array: for every `roles` entry that is a worker claim (`"issue" in claim`) with `typeof claim.pendingAssignment === "string"`, replace it with `{ kind, task }` where kind is `catchup` iff `JSON.parse(task)` (inside try/catch; a parse failure means `assignment`) is a record whose `type === "catchup-worker"`; leave every other claim, every non-string pendingAssignment, and controller claims untouched; return `{ ...rest, version: 25, roles }`. Doc comment states the rule in one sentence.

Add `export function isActivePhase(state: LegionState, issue: IssueKey, role: string): boolean { const phase = state.phases[issue]; return phase !== undefined && !phase.completed && phase.phase === role; }`.

Tests: bump every `version: 24` / `.toBe(24)` expectation and every test title naming the chain end (`... and v24`, `initializes empty v24 state`, `rejects a v24 locator`) to 25. New test `migrates v24 state to v25 by classifying each persisted pendingAssignment string by its payload`: a v24 file with an implementer claim `pendingAssignment: "implement #43"`, a tester claim `pendingAssignment: JSON.stringify({ type: "catchup-worker", unhandled: [] })`, a reviewer claim with no pendingAssignment, and the controller claim; expect `{ kind: "assignment", task: "implement #43" }`, `{ kind: "catchup", task: <that JSON> }`, the other two `toEqual` their inputs, `migrated.version === 25`, and `<file>.v24.bak` equal to the raw input. New test: a v25 file whose claim carries a bare-string `pendingAssignment` is rejected with `/Invalid Legion state/` (strict schema, never a silent fallback). Fix the v19 -> v20 test's `pendingAssignment: "verify #41"` expectation per concerns.

tasks.title: Daemon AGENTS.md (Acceptance 6)
steps: Row `POST /legion/v1/worker/started`: append `Never writes the issue's active phase (state.phases[issue]); a registration for a role that is not the active phase and has no queued assignment logs one line and changes nothing else.`
Row `POST /legion/v1/worker/ready`: `pendingAssignment` is `{ kind: "assignment" | "catchup", task }`; delivering an `assignment` makes the role the issue's active phase; a `catchup` does not.

Operational invariant bullet starting `spawn_worker always resumes the same agent for an existing phase`: append the rule -- `state.phases[issue]` is written by exactly one thing, the delivery of an architect assignment (`promptExistingWorker` with `kind: "assignment"`, prompted straight into a live worker or delivered from the claim's `pendingAssignment` at `/worker/ready`); a bare `/worker/started`, a reconnect, and the daemon's own `catchup-worker` prompt (`resumeWorker`) never write it. A catch-up is not sent to a phase-worker role that is neither the active phase nor holding a pending assignment (a sub-architect is always eligible: it parks for the life of its subtree and has no other recovery path), and never replaces a pending architect assignment (dropped with one log line, checked again inside the role's lock). The phase changes on a relaunch only through the architect's next `spawn_worker`.
